<reason>B won the live comparison: a cap’s savings accrue to remaining revolvers while the opening’s own desperate borrowers are the ones priced out toward worse substitutes or no liquidity. A was punchier and correctly noted the motion’s “even if,” but treated stipulated access loss as a reason not to weigh substitution and never showed remaining-borrower gains dominate. Clipped B opening/closing kept the margin modest.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.3–B2.5: fringe lenders already serve the uncarded, so a binding cap expands that pool rather than leaving substitution unchanged—and the leaked borrowers are exactly the population A claimed to protect.</best_rebuttal>
